source_version: Theory of Computing15(2019),Article16; final publisher source December14,2019
title: Approximate polynomial satisfiability is NP-hard and lies in PSPACE

standard_prerequisites.name: Affine/projective algebraic geometry, arithmetic circuits and space complexity
standard_prerequisites.statement: Original prerequisite statements/citations and full source-local fiber, projection, curve and circuit constructions retained.
standard_prerequisites.use: No collector reproof or field/complexity strengthening. Original input encodings and finite-field scope remain explicit.

core_obligations: The authors connect infinitesimal solutions to zero in the Zariski closure of a polynomial-map image, then reduce image dimension by random projection and hyperplane cutting while preserving the zero-membership question. Perron/annihilator bounds and the complete polynomial-space enumeration and correctness argument are retained. Original NP-hardness and PSPACE claims are one target.

NNL/e.s.o.p. consequences, stronger SBP questions and characteristic-zero GRH questions are not extra counts.
